graft.title: Found pytest checks: the venv of the pyproject they sit under, and `off` taking effect
graft.need: (1) The tests tend finds in Python test files run `pytest bindings/python/tests/test_X.py` from the repo root, which has no pytest; the interpreter should be the .venv beside the nearest pyproject.toml above the file (here bindings/python/.venv), run from that directory. A package built by maturin also needs `maturin develop` first, so where the extension isn't built the found test can't pass on its own: a declared test covering the same directory could stand in for the found ones. (2) In autodyne batch 01a1c1e4-5ba4 I declared each of the six found tests with `off: true` and a reason; `tend code checks` still lists all six under autodyne / Python bindings as FAILED and design_review counts them as broken. A found test declared off should be off, as an outer node's is.
graft.use_case: autodyne's declared `pytest` check (build the extension in bindings/python/.venv, run all six files: 227 passed, 1 skipped) is the real test; the six found ones fail in 0.5 s without running anything and keep the project's requirements from reading clean.

answer.text: Both are bugs. Planned: a found Python test runs with the .venv of the nearest pyproject.toml above it, from that folder (not the repo root's), and a found test declared with off: true is off for tend code checks and design_review, as the claim that a declared test takes a found one's place already says. Your declared pytest check stays the real test meanwhile.
